```{r setup}
library(quant2qual)
```

The engine only ever sees three standardised dimensions. What makes a narrative
read like a usability case study rather than a learner profile or a
response-quality audit is **vocabulary** and **interpretation**, and both live
in a domain pack.

```{r domains}
q2q_domains()
```

All three packs share one rule geometry, named in their own terms:

| Signature | UX | Learning | Survey |
|---|---|---|---|
| Obstructed persistence | Frustrated Fighter | Struggling Persister | Effortful Struggler |
| Early exit under friction | Frustrated Novice | At-Risk Withdrawer | Careless Speeder |
| Deliberate depth | Methodical Explorer | Deep Learner | Deliberative Responder |
| Fluent expertise | Power Navigator | Efficient Achiever | Efficient Responder |
| Shallow contact | Passive Disengaged | Surface Engager | Minimal Responder |
| Cohort-typical | Baseline User | Steady Learner | Typical Responder |

## Learning analytics

```{r learning}
learners <- mock_behavioral_data(180, domain = "learning")
lp <- identify_archetype(learners, domain = "learning")
summary(lp)
generate_narrative(lp, select_cases(lp, archetypes = "At-Risk Withdrawer"), style = "ux")
```

## Survey paradata and response quality

In the survey pack, *friction* is the number of failed attention and
consistency checks, and the interpretation draws on the satisficing and
insufficient-effort-responding literature. Note how it distinguishes a fast
respondent who writes well and passes checks (*Efficient Responder*) from one
who is fast, terse and fails them (*Careless Speeder*): speed alone is not
treated as poor quality.

```{r survey}
resp <- mock_behavioral_data(250, domain = "survey")
sp <- identify_archetype(resp, domain = "survey", scaling = "robust")
generate_narrative(sp, select_cases(sp, archetypes = "Careless Speeder"))
```

## Adapting the vocabulary

A lexicon can be overridden piece by piece. Here the UX pack is adapted to a
study of clinicians using an electronic health record:

```{r lexicon}
ehr <- q2q_lexicon(
  "ux",
  subject = "the clinician", subject_short = "clinician", subject_plural = "clinicians",
  case_label = "Clinician Profile",
  dimensions = list(intensity = list(noun = "order-entry activity", unit = "orders")),
  pace = list(noun = "ordering rate", unit = "orders per minute"),
  rate = list(noun = "alert rate", unit = "alerts per 100 orders")
)
ehr
```

Pass it when classifying, so that the narratives and reports use it throughout:

```{r ehr}
p <- identify_archetype(mock_behavioral_data(150), lexicon = ehr)
generate_narrative(p, 104, style = "ux")
```

## Your own column names

The defaults come from the lexicon, but any columns can be mapped:

```{r columns}
logs <- data.frame(
  session = sprintf("S%03d", 1:60),
  seconds = round(stats::rlnorm(60, log(600), 0.5)),
  taps = stats::rpois(60, 80),
  crashes = stats::rpois(60, 1)
)
p <- identify_archetype(logs, velocity = "seconds", intensity = "taps",
                        friction = "crashes", id = "session",
                        lexicon = q2q_lexicon("ux", dimensions = list(
                          velocity = list(unit = "seconds"),
                          intensity = list(unit = "taps"),
                          friction = list(noun = "app crashes", unit = "crashes"))))
generate_narrative(p, "S001", style = "brief")
```
